text:
Morgan Lee: Quick follow-up from yesterday's RFC on Private/VPC networking — we need to decide control plane topology for Private customers. Two choices on the table: 1) fully Redwood-managed control plane (hosted, peered to customer VPCs or PrivateLink), 2) customer-managed control plane inside the customer's VPC that talks to Redwood runtime via a minimal API endpoint. Pros/cons?

Kevin Patel: I lean towards hosted control plane with PrivateLink endpoints for customers who want no public egress. Easier ops, faster feature rollout.

Anya Cho: Agree on ops. But hosted CP means we must be very careful about metadata leakage and audit surfaces. Some SOC2/IL/regulated customers will insist on CP in their account.

Raj Singh: For the hybrid case, what about a split-control approach: control plane config + rollout commands stay hosted, but sensitive keys/audit logs live in customer account via S3/KMS replication?

Morgan Lee: Split-control is interesting. Tradeoffs: higher operational complexity and more code paths + test surface. But may satisfy strict compliance. Has anyone sketched network diagrams for both approaches?

Kevin Patel: I drew a quick sketch last night. Short version: hosted CP -> customers use AWS PrivateLink or peering to reach a regional control endpoint. Runtime traffic can be routed separately to dedicated capacity in customer VPC when Private option is selected.

Kevin Patel: For peering we have to handle IP overlap and routing. PrivateLink avoids that but costs more per endpoint. Also PrivateLink doesn't support cross-region.

Anya Cho: Note: PrivateLink is only for ENI in the customer's account — we can do interface endpoints to our NLB. If we go that route, we should restrict the control-plane APIs to only management operations (no payloads). Runtime should never traverse the hosted control plane for PII-sensitive jobs.

Raj Singh: Example terraform snippet for endpoint service I mocked:

```
resource "aws_vpc_endpoint_service" "cp_service" {
  acceptance_required = false
  network_load_balancer_arns = [aws_lb.cp_lb.arn]
}
resource "aws_vpc_endpoint" "customer_cp_ep" {
  vpc_id = var.customer_vpc_id
  service_name = aws_vpc_endpoint_service.cp_service.service_name
  vpc_endpoint_type = "Interface"
}
```

Morgan Lee: Nice. Also thinking about failure modes: if hosted CP is down, customer control plane operations (rollouts, scaling) are impacted. For dedicated/private runtime, we must support local fallback — e.g., local autoscaler runs without CP until reconnection.

Kevin Patel: That implies an agent in customer VPC with a small control loop + signed offline op queue. When CP reconnects it reconciles. It's doable but we need signing and replay resistance.

Anya Cho: Security: if we allow peering, we need a flow for granting and revoking routes and SG rules programmatically. Might need ORCA-style short-lived peering tokens or a provisioning service. Manual peering is slow for onboarding.

Raj Singh: Could use Transit Gateway for customers with many VPCs, but TGW costs are high and customers may already have it. Support both peering and PrivateLink and let the customer choose. Default to PrivateLink for smaller customers.

Morgan Lee: Operational checklist ideas: onboarding playbook, IAM/KMS patterns, CP must log all operations to customer audit sink, and we need a strongly-typed minimal API for CP-to-runtime commands. Also SLA expectations when CP is managed vs unmanaged.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: created stub branch redwood/private-cp-agent-prototype -> PR #428

Kevin Patel: For the API contract: keep it versioned and opt-in. Suggest RPCs: RegisterRuntime, Heartbeat, RequestRollout, FetchConfig, FetchSecretsMeta. No model payloads. Everything authenticated with mTLS + client certs stored in KMS in customer account (if private).

Anya Cho: Also we should define network egress requirements for telemetry: minimal telemetry can be proxied via the CP, but for regulated customers send telemetry to customer-owned endpoints (Datadog/Splunk) inside their VPC.

Raj Singh: Action items: (1) I'll draft a short network diagram doc (peering, PrivateLink, TGW) and list costs/limits; (2) Kevin, can you sketch the offline agent (signing/queue) and failure semantics? (3) Anya, security checklist + audit wire protocol.

Morgan Lee: Thanks. Let's reconvene Friday 10am to pick defaults and decide whether to fold split-control into MVP. Please drop links to diagrams in this thread before EOD Thursday. :thumbsup:
